title: Determinantal weight
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $(p,q,k_0,k)$ and the coefficient convention
$\ell\ne p$, $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell\subset\Qlb$ of
[def-weil-finite-field-fiber], and fix a field isomorphism
$\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$.
Let $X_0$ be a curve over $k_0$ [def-pc-curve] which is normal
(its local rings are integrally closed domains, in the terminology of
[def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]) and geometrically connected
[def-weil-geometric-hypotheses].
Let $\mathcal V$ be an irreducible lisse $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf on $X_0$,
with Weil fundamental representation $V$ of
[def-wf-fundamental-representation]. Here lisse sheaves and finite-stage
coefficients are as in [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves] and
[def-wf-weil-category], and irreducibility is as in
[def-real-weil-representation-operations]: $V$ is nonzero and has no
nonzero proper Weil-stable subspace. Write
$r=\dim_{\Qlb}V>0$ for its rank.

Choose a finite coefficient field $\Ql\subseteq E\subset\Qlb$
over which its representation is defined; finite coefficient fields
are the elements of [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set].
Let $a\in\mathbf R$ be the unique number supplied by
[lem-wf-determinantal-weight-exists], for which the determinant line
$\det(\mathcal V)$ of [def-mg-determinant-line] is punctually
$\iota$-pure of weight $a$ in the sense of [def-weil-punctual-weights].
The *determinantal weight* is the real number

$$
\dw_\iota(\mathcal V):=\frac{a}{r}.
$$

Well-definedness with respect to the finite coefficient field is supplied
by [lem-wf-determinantal-weight-coefficient-field]. We use the same
notation $\dw_\iota(V)$ for the associated representation.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $X_0$ be a normal geometrically connected curve over $k_0$, fix
$\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$, and let $\mathcal V$ be an
irreducible lisse Weil sheaf of rank $r$. Choose a finite coefficient
field over which its representation is defined, and let $a$ be the
weight of [lem-wf-determinantal-weight-exists], so that the
determinant line
$\det(\mathcal V)$ is
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight
$a$. The *determinantal weight* of $\mathcal V$ is

$$
\dw_\iota(\mathcal V):=\frac{a}{r}.
$$

We use the same
notation for the associated representation $V$.
This number does not depend on the chosen finite coefficient field, by
[lem-wf-determinantal-weight-coefficient-field].
